newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait mulls gradual cut of state foreign workers.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait mulls gradual cut of state foreign workers.

text.p: Kuwait is considering an annual 10 percent cut in the number of foreigners hired by the state to create jobs for its nationals, an official said on Monday.
"The cabinet has been presented with a study that recommends a 10 percent cut in (state) expatriate workers" annually, said a planning ministry official.
"The purpose of the reduction would be to provide jobs for Kuwaiti graduates. The reduction would affect some jobs more than others depending on the number of graduates in each area."

Kuwait needs to provide about 10,000 potential graduates with jobs in each of the coming five years, the official said. Currently some 3,000 Kuwaitis -- or 1.75 of Kuwait's national workforce of about 173,000 -- is unemployed.

Some 40 percent of the 250,000 state-hired workers are foreigners, mainly from Asian and other Arab countries. They also hold nearly all of the 616,000 private-sector jobs, most of which are not attractive to Kuwaiti workers.
Kuwait is home to 720,000 nationals and about 1.25 million foreigners.
